title: Runtime and image publication
current: Main factories attest wheels and native images before tag promotion of identical bytes. Server images, offline release wheelhouses and bridge installs use uv.lock; dependency upgrades go through uv lock --upgrade in a reviewed PR. Native image and wheelhouse checks reject third-party version drift, and the container data test requires CPython 3.13 Linux wheels for both architectures. New tags, wheels, images, pins and display share BASE.YYYYMMDDHHMM from the exact commit UTC committer minute, without prefixes or local segments. Installed-package readers use generic PEP 440. Artifact promotion and image publication emit GitHub Actions error annotations on refusal so release failure traces retain the named cause and recovery. Main server-image builds write architecture-specific GHCR BuildKit product cache refs in mode=max that share image blobs and retain the UV tools and declared build-backend environment; queue checks only read them. CI container GHA caches write only from main. Stable runtime ancestry includes locked external dependencies and the checksum-verified PostgreSQL operation, so image and cache share both. PostgreSQL precedes workspace manifests and mounts only its transitive source inputs; unrelated client edits do not invalidate it. Writable source bind mounts discard source copies and wheel build scratch; only the four product wheels leave the builder. The independent tools-based builder runs all four package builds concurrently with the manifests’ exact backends already installed, disables per-package build isolation, builds offline and waits for every result before completeness validation; runtime dependency and PostgreSQL layer loading can overlap wheel production. The root development wheel and runtime test tree do not ship; exact package selection and a build gate enforce that. Temporary wheels use stored ZIP entries to avoid compression before installation; image and registry-cache export use gzip level one. Pip and UV download caches stay out of exported build layers. Dependency and workspace bytecode is compiled during installation; runtime installs only workspace wheels over the stable dependency venv. Build identity follows stable OS/user/client/dependency layers. Installed-module validation runs before bundle rendering in one process so imports are reused; both checks always execute and both must pass. The evidence tool's --diagnostics reports retained BuildKit vertex durations; acceptance still measures the full native build/push step against the fixed ten-run baseline and requires thirty seconds of median improvement across ten corrected main runs.
desired: Complete real consumer CI and coordinated activation after required existing-format releases. Record artifact equality and release-time improvement. Dormant installs reinstall instead of adding old-version bridges.
